presentingComplaint: 2 days of fever with dysuria, frequency and left flank pain
history: 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and benign prostatic hyperplasia presents with 2 days of high-grade fever with rigors, dysuria, increased urinary frequency and left loin pain. Reports poor urinary stream and incomplete voiding for months. Received a course of oral antibiotics 6 weeks ago for a similar episode. No recent hospitalization or indwelling catheter. Non-smoker, HbA1c 8.9% at last review.
examination: Ill-looking but alert and oriented. Left costovertebral angle tenderness. Suprapubic mild tenderness. Palpable non-tender bladder suggesting incomplete emptying. No rash, no meningism. Chest clear, abdomen soft with no guarding or organomegaly. Peripheries warm, capillary refill <2s.

labs.Urinalysis: leucocyte esterase +++, nitrites positive, >100 WBC/hpf, many bacteria

imaging: Renal ultrasound: mild left hydronephrosis, post-void residual 210 mL, enlarged prostate; no perinephric collection or abscess
microbiology: Urine culture and blood cultures sent; Gram-negative bacilli on urine Gram stain (E. coli grown on culture, pending sensitivities)
differentialDiagnoses: Acute pyelonephritis in a complicated host
finalDiagnosis: Complicated urinary tract infection (febrile UTI with obstructive uropathy/BPH and diabetes in a male)
citations: Harrison 22e — Urinary Tract Infections, Pyelonephritis, and Prostatitis
IDSA Complicated Intra-abdominal/Urinary Tract Infection guidance; IDSA Catheter-Associated and Complicated UTI 2010
stewardship: Empiric IV ceftriaxone 1-2 g daily (or piperacillin-tazobactam if ESBL risk factors) covering Enterobacterales; de-escalate to oral agent per culture sensitivities. Total 10-14 days given complicating factors (male sex, obstruction, diabetes). Relieve obstruction/ensure adequate bladder drainage.
contraindications: Beta-lactam/cephalosporin allergy — use aztreonam or fluoroquinolone alternative
Avoid nitrofurantoin (inadequate tissue/renal penetration for febrile/complicated UTI and reduced efficacy with eGFR impairment)
Renal dose-adjust and monitor creatinine given AKI and diabetes
edgeCases: Prior antibiotics within 90 days raise ESBL-producing E. coli risk — escalate to carbapenem if severe or ESBL confirmed
Failure to relieve obstruction (hydronephrosis/high residual) can precipitate urosepsis despite appropriate antibiotics
In men, febrile UTI frequently reflects concurrent prostatic involvement requiring longer therapy
expectedMaiK: Febrile UTI with pyuria/nitrites plus a complicating factor (male sex, diabetes, BPH with obstruction, prior antibiotics) defines a complicated UTI; empiric coverage should target Enterobacterales with attention to ESBL risk, and source control by relieving the obstruction is essential alongside antibiotics.
expectedNextQuestions: Is there complete inability to void or worsening loin pain suggesting obstruction requiring drainage?
expectedInvestigations: Urine culture with sensitivities and blood cultures
Renal tract ultrasound / CT to exclude obstruction or abscess and measure post-void residual

crossAccept.rationale: Pyelonephritis is a form of complicated UTI; overlapping systemic-abx mgmt.

regressionAssertions: stewardship tier is not null and antibiotics include an Enterobacterales-active beta-lactam
